subject: ggplot2 feature request - scale specific eas, i.e. fontsize

messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: ggplot2 feature request - scale specific eas, i.e. fontsize
parts:
Hi,

Sometimes I want to vary an aesthetic independently per geom type,
for instance:

(point) size
linewidth
fontsize

In these cases, I'd like to be able to say, for instance:

stat_summary(geom=c('text','line','point'), aes(
size=x,
fontsize=I(10),
linesize=4))

In this instance, the base aes is read by point, but text
recognises that a specific size aes is available and uses that
instead. this can either be variable or fixed for that scaletype.

variable:

qplot(data=x,fontsize=n,size=mean,geom=c("text","point"))

fixed:

qplot(data=X,fontsize=I(10),size=height,geom=c("text","point"))

-Alex

>
> fixed:
>
> qplot(data=X,fontsize=I(10),size=height,geom=c("text","point"))

Use ggplot() + geom_*** and you can easily achieve that:

ggplot(data=x) + geom_point(aes(size=x)) + geom_text(aes(), size=10, linesize=4)

everything you put inside aes is "mapped" to the data, everything outside aes is set as an absolute value.

parts:
This falls down for stat_thing() classes. The private output
variables they make, such as ..y.. are not available in subsequent
geoms.

This is perfect:

> qplot(data=mtcars, cyl, mpg, size=5, label=..y.., stat="summary", fun.y=mean, geom=c("point","text"))

I'd like to specify point and font-size separately... so I split into
geoms:

> qplot(data=mtcars, cyl, mpg, size=5, label=..y.., stat="summary", fun.y=mean)+geom_text()

Now the text is printed for EACH y, not for the summarised y.

If I could separate the aesthetics I would use

> qplot(data=mtcars, cyl, mpg, pointsize=5, fontsize=8, label=..y.., stat="summary", fun.y=mean, geom=c("point","text"))

or similar.

-Alex

On 2012-Mar-16, at 18:22 , Alex@775 wrote:
>
> Now the text is printed for EACH y, not for the summarised y.
>
> If I could separate the aesthetics I would use
>
>> qplot(data=mtcars, cyl, mpg, pointsize=5, fontsize=8, label=..y.., stat="summary", fun.y=mean, geom=c("point","text"))
>
> or similar.

It seems you want:

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x=cyl, y=mpg)) +
geom_point(stat="summary", fun.y=mean, size=5) +
geom_text(stat="summary", fun.y=mean, mapping=aes(label=..y..), size=3, vjust=-1)

The stat argument is not inherited from the ggplot call to each layer (i.e. each geom) so you have to repeat it, and then you can customize the rest independently in each geom (while making sure that values that you want to *set*, rather than map, as the size here, are specified outside of the aes call.

>
> Should this convo really be in Dev? I'm not an existing contributor

Yes you might want to move this to ggplot-dev.

Ultimately it's for Hadley to decide but I would guess the change needed to get this working in a general manner is not trivial.

In addition, from a user perspective, it complicates the interface to have several names for the same aesthetic (size and pointsize for point, size and textsize for text etc.).
Furthermore, still from a UX perspective, I always thought that the "true" ggplot syntax is the ggplot + geom one. qplot is just a shorthand, for quick jobs and/or to make users of the base plot somewhat at home. So you can't ask qplot to do everything that ggplot + geom does, otherwise, it would become too complicated and defeat its purpose of being a quick, simple shorthand.

But again, that's only my point of view and only Hadley can really say what he wants qplot to be.

Answers inline

-Alex Brown

On Mar 19, 2012, at 1:00 PM, Jean-Olivier Irisson <iri...@normalesup.org> wrote:
> In addition, from a user perspective, it complicates the interface to have several names for the same aesthetic (size and pointsize for point, size and textsize for text etc.).
I would argue quite strongly that they are NOT the same aesthetic at all, in fact I'd prefer if there was no common name.  However, that would break backward compatibility.

> Furthermore, still from a UX perspective, I always thought that the "true" ggplot syntax is the ggplot + geom one. qplot is just a shorthand, for quick jobs and/or to make users of the base plot somewhat at home. So you can't ask qplot to do everything that ggplot + geom does, otherwise, it would become too complicated and defeat its purpose of being a quick, simple shorthand.
I was only using qplot for compactness.  However, you should note that the stat_ methods, and the layer method accept multiple geoms.
> But again, that's only my point of view and only Hadley can really say what he wants qplot to be.

And a valid one.  I use ggplot a lot, and I love it, and want to make it easier for new users and maintainers to understand and use it.  As part of this I want to file off the sharp edges that have hit me and every new user.  The aesthetic issue is only one of them (and probably quite private to me).

-Alex
